newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says Israeli clampdown "counter-productive". [CORRECTED 10:17 GMT 9/8]
newsitem.headline: EU says Israeli clampdown "counter-productive". [CORRECTED 10:17 GMT 9/8]

text.p: The European Union said on Friday it would express its concern to Israel over "excessive and counter-productive" measures introduced in the wake of last month's suicide bombings in a Jerusalem market.

"The EU has decided to ask its representatives in Tel Aviv to make a demarche to (Israeli) Foreign Minister (David) Levy to make our concern known," Luxembourg Foreign Minister (corrects from Prime Minister) Jacques Poos said in a letter to Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.

"The European Union fully shares your concern about the disastrous effect of the measures decided by the Israeli government...many of these...are new and seem to be excessive," wrote Poos, whose country currently holds the rotating presidency of the 15-nation EU.

Poos, replying to a plea from Arafat to intervene and block some of the Israeli measures, said the Palestinian population was being punished, although its responsibility for the Jerusalem bombings, which killed 13, had not been established.

The EU was last month instrumental in bringing together Arafat and Levy for talks in Brussels in a bid to revive the stalled Middle East peace process, but any progress there was overshadowed by the bombings.
"The European Union will remain committed to the peace process. It will remain entirely at the disposal of both parties in order to assist them in (its) resumption," Poos said. REUTER
